newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Sanofi's Hungary unit pays 96 dividend of $29.8mln.
newsitem.headline: Sanofi's Hungary unit pays 96 dividend of $29.8mln.

text.p: Chinoin Rt, the Hungarian drug maker unit of French Sanofi group, decided on Saturday to pay a dividend of 5.4 billion forints ($29.8 million) on 1996 earnings, the Hungarian MTI news agency said.
Most of the dividend will go to Sanofi, which holds a 98.7 percent stake in Chinoin, MTI said.
Chinoin shareholders held their annual meeting on Saturday.
MTI quoted Chinoin chief executive officer Miklos Gyorgy as saying the company paid a high dividend to ensure a satisfactory return on Sanofi's investments in Chinoin, which totalled $200 million.
Chinoin will pay a dividend of 18,500 forints per share, compared with 5,000 forints per share paid on the 1995 profit, MTI said.
Gyorgy said Chinoin boosted its turnover by 33 percent to 29.44 billion forints ($162.5 million) in 1996, accounting for 6.5 percent of the total sales of Sanofi group.
Chinoin's exports totalled 15.4 billion forints ($85 million) in 1996 and it posted an after-tax profit of 7.67 billion forints ($42.36 million), he added.
